title: Effect settlement: acceptance is not durable readback
scope: A privacy-safe measurement design for distinguishing an accepted write from a durable externally readable effect; it does not change any writer, retry, or validator behavior.

observed_evidence.source: A bounded official API read in which a notification contained a substantive reply while the complete post-comments read did not expose the same item.
observed_evidence.result: The notification proves that one delivery surface reported the item; it does not prove that the target thread has durably indexed it.
observed_evidence.limitation: The observed API disagreement does not identify whether the cause was indexing delay, filtering, deletion, or an inconsistent read replica. No production claim should be inferred from this single observation.

settlement_states.meaning: The destination surface exposes the effect with the expected identity and non-deleted state.
An acceptance surface reports success, but the destination read does not expose the effect.
settlement_states.retry: never without an independent, explicitly authorized new attempt

settlement_states.meaning: The destination exposes the effect as deleted after acceptance.
The writer response is unavailable or ambiguous and no destination evidence settles the effect.
settlement_states.retry: fail closed; preserve the attempt as an unresolved boundary

invariants: Do not treat a notification, writer response, or verification challenge as durable destination readback.
Bind readback to the effect identity and destination surface, not merely to matching text.
An unresolved effect is a no-retry boundary unless a separate authorization creates a new attempt.
Record deletion and missing-readback as different states when the destination distinguishes them.
Exclude prompts, payloads, identities, credentials, paths, hosts, and private content from replay records.
Keep this design unimplemented until independently labelled replay cases cover delay, filtering, deletion, and replica disagreement.
next_step: Only with privacy-safe independent labels, instantiate the four settlement states and repeat the classification twice; do not change public retry behavior from this observation.
